verdict.rationale: Lium's SDK can run a function on an ephemeral GPU node and remove the pod afterward, so you pay nothing once the job ends. That is a serverless-like, scale-to-zero pattern for one-off jobs, but it is not an autoscaling worker pool. The rest of the product is pod rental with TTL or spend-cap auto-deletion. Missing for 10: autoscaling worker pools that scale with request load, persistent serverless endpoints or queues, cold-start and scaling configuration, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy code to autoscaling serverless GPU workers that scale to zero, instead of managing always-on instances

citations.quote: The SDK rents the cheapest matching node, runs the function there, returns the result and removes the pod (or keeps it warm).
Your agent starts a pod, runs the job and removes it, within a budget you set.
